$comment: Banner sections of each 2.1.1 reference entry, in file order, and the femto files (relative to css/) that replace each one in a hybrid build. Owned by the refs agent; see tests/reference/README.md.
banner_format: A banner is the three or more lines '/**', ' * <title>' (one or more title lines), ' */'. 'title' is the first title line exactly as written; 'banner' is every title line. 'line' is the 1-based line of '/**' in the reference file. A section runs from its banner to the line before the next banner (or end of file). The '(preamble)' pseudo-section is everything before the first banner (@charset and the copyright comment); it has no femto files.

sections.title: Grid
banner: Minimal grid system with auto-layout columns

themes.$comment: Every theme reference has exactly the same banner titles and order as its entry (checked when this file was generated). In 2.1.1 they also sit at the same lines (only the trailing newline differs), but locate them by title rather than relying on that. Azure is built into tokens/, so femto.css itself is the azure reference.

options.$comment: Option references are compiled on the default entry only and have the default entry's banner titles and order (checked when this file was generated), at different line numbers.

notes.note: The Styles section also holds declarations that serve class rules of later modules: --femto-grid-column-gap and --femto-grid-row-gap in the first :root, :host block; 'a.secondary, a.contrast { --femto-text-decoration: underline }'; 'details.dropdown summary:not([role=button])' and 'nav details.dropdown summary:focus-visible' (--femto-outline-width); and two '[role=search]:has(... .secondary:focus ...), [role=group]:has(...)' and '.contrast' rules (--femto-group-box-shadow-focus-with-button). Moving them into the files of the modules they serve (layout/grid.css, content/link.css, components/dropdown.css, components/group.css) would put them later in the cascade than 2.1.1 does.

For the six light-primary themes (amber, grey, lime, pumpkin, sand, yellow; --femto-primary-inverse: #000) the Styles rule '[aria-busy=true]...:not(.outline)::before' becomes 'filter: brightness(0) invert(0)' instead of invert(1) in femto.<color>.css. The neighbouring 'details summary[role=button]:not(.outline)::after' keeps invert(1) in every theme. This is the 28th theme-dependent declaration. femto has neither filter: components/accordion.css and components/loading.css draw the chevron and the spinner as masks filled with currentColor on these buttons, so both follow the button's text color in every theme and scheme.

notes.topic: where the option references change Styles
notes.note: Both responsive options live in the Styles section: options/femto.fixed-typography.css drops the five '@media (min-width: ...) { :root, :host { --femto-font-size: ... } }' blocks right after the first :root block; options/femto.responsive-spacings.css inserts five media blocks for 'body > header, body > main, body > footer, section' and five for 'article' (--femto-block-spacing-vertical/horizontal) at the same place. An appended options/*.css file sits at the end of the cascade instead; the hybrid build will show whether that order matters.

Every non-azure theme changes 7 tokens in each of the 3 scheme blocks (light; media dark; [data-theme=dark]): --femto-text-selection-color, --femto-primary, --femto-primary-background, --femto-primary-underline, --femto-primary-hover, --femto-primary-hover-background, --femto-primary-focus (21 declarations). The six light-primary themes also change --femto-primary-inverse (#fff -> #000) and --femto-switch-thumb-box-shadow (0 0 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) -> 0 0 0.5rem rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25)) in each block (6 more), plus the Styles filter above: 28 in all. No other section depends on the theme color.

The scheme blocks also hold declarations for class-based components: five --femto-dropdown-* tokens (background-color, border-color, box-shadow, color, hover-background-color) in each scheme block, and in both dark blocks 'details summary[role=button].contrast:not(.outline)::after' and '[aria-busy=true]...contrast...:not(.outline)::before' { filter: brightness(0) }. femto has no such filters (see the Styles note on the theme-color-dependent declaration). Moving the dropdown tokens to components/dropdown.css would put them later in the cascade than 2.1.1 does.

2.1.1 writes the light block as '[data-theme=light], :root:not([data-theme=dark]), :host(:not([data-theme=dark]))', the dark media block as '@media only screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme]), :host(:not([data-theme])) }', and '[data-theme=dark]'. femto's tokens/schemes.css keeps both :host() forms and the screen media type, as '@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)': 'only' hid the query from browsers that predate media queries and has no effect in femto's. Without 'screen', print output with a dark OS preference turns dark where 2.1.1 stays light; without :host(), shadow roots lose their scheme.

Besides the three token blocks the section has, per scheme, 'input:is([type=submit], [type=button], [type=reset], [type=checkbox], [type=radio], [type=file])' { --femto-form-element-focus-color: var(--femto-primary-focus) } under each scheme selector, the --femto-icon-valid and --femto-icon-invalid data-URI tokens, which stay per scheme, and at its very end an unscoped 'progress, [type=checkbox], [type=radio], [type=range] { accent-color: var(--femto-primary) }'.

notes.topic: class rules in the middle of a section
notes.note: Link: the .secondary and .contrast rules sit before 'a[role=button] { display: inline-block }'. Button: .secondary, .contrast and .outline rules are interleaved with element rules. Modal: '.close' is merged into the same selector lists as ':is(a, button)[rel=prev]' (3 rules), and the .modal-is-open and .modal-is-opening/.modal-is-closing rules and the modal-overlay and modal keyframes sit in the same section. Table: the 'table.striped' rule closes the section. Each of these sections maps to one file (content/link.css, content/button.css, content/table.css, components/modal.css), so the class rules keep their 2.1.1 place among the element rules.

The 19 css/pico.<color>.css files came from scripts/build-themes.js (sass.compile, whose 'outputStyle' option is ignored, so the output is expanded) and, unlike css/pico.css, end without a trailing newline. Their banners match the default entry's exactly.

notes.topic: no-transitions reference removes more than durations
notes.note: $enable-transitions: false keeps '--femto-transition: 0.2s ease-in-out' defined but drops every 'transition' declaration (including the -webkit-/-moz-/-ms- copies in the range track and thumb and progress pseudo-element rules, and the switch thumb's 'transition: margin 0.1s ease-in-out'), the modal animation rules (.modal-is-opening/.modal-is-closing) with the modal-overlay and modal keyframes, and every tooltip slide animation with its keyframes and --femto-tooltip-slide-to/--femto-tooltip-caret-slide-to tokens. An options/no-transitions.css that only sets '--femto-transition: 0s' leaves transition-property lists, modal animations and tooltip animations in place, so those show up as differences.
